The first impact shakes the gatehouse to its foundations.

You brace yourself against the ballista platform as the leading bone-beast slams into the outer barricade. Its enormous skull strikes the timber with enough force to split a support beam. Soldiers stumble backwards, and a shower of splinters scatters across the wall-walk.

“Hold your positions!” Commander Vane roars.

You move towards the nearest ballista. Its heavy wooden frame is reinforced with iron bands, and the firing mechanism is already loaded with a thick cold-iron bolt. Two soldiers stand at the cranks, waiting for the order to fire.

Beyond the walls, the siege-beasts advance through the fog.

There are three in the first wave. Each is larger than a horse, assembled from interlocking bones and wrapped in jagged plates of obsidian armour. Violet light pulses between their ribs, holding their unnatural bodies together. Behind them, the Bone Coven's ward-breakers move in disciplined formations, carrying long staves and hooked instruments designed to disrupt the garrison's protective runes.

“They're using the beasts to draw our fire,” you shout.

Vane turns towards you.

“Explain.”

“The ward-breakers are staying behind them. They're waiting for us to waste our bolts on the armour. Once we're reloading, they'll have time to attack the gate's protective wards.”

Vane looks towards the advancing ranks.

“Then we make every shot count.”

He points towards the largest beast.

“Take that one down before it reaches the gate!”

You climb onto the firing platform and look through the narrow sighting frame. The fog shifts constantly, obscuring the creature's movements. The wind blows across the valley from the north, carrying smoke and ash towards the battlements.

The ballista crew wait for your instruction.

“Not yet,” you say.

The beast lowers its skull and charges.

Its claws tear through the frozen earth. The ground shakes beneath its weight, and the soldiers along the wall begin shouting as it closes the distance.

You watch the movement of the fog, judging the wind and the creature's speed. A shot fired too early will strike the ground. One fired too late may hit the beast's armour without penetrating.

“Wait for it!”

The creature raises its head.

“Now!”

The soldiers release the mechanism.

The ballista launches its bolt with a thunderous crack. The heavy projectile cuts through the fog, striking the beast's shoulder. Cold iron flashes against obsidian, and a burst of violet energy erupts from the wound.

The creature staggers but does not fall.

“Reload!” Vane shouts.

A second bolt is dragged into position. The ward-breakers behind the beast raise their staves, and the air begins to vibrate with a low, unnatural hum.

You recognise the pattern.

They are trying to reinforce the creature before the damage can spread.

“Target the ward-breakers!” you shout. “They're holding the magic together!”

Vane follows your line of sight.

“Ballista crews, shift your aim!”

The first volley misses as the fog thickens. A bolt disappears into the grey haze, and another strikes the earth short of its target.

The ward-breakers continue advancing.

One raises an obsidian staff, and a violet ring spreads across the ground beneath the leading beast. Its broken shoulder begins to knit together, bones dragging back into place.

You grip the wooden rail.

“Again. Aim higher. The wind is pushing the bolts left.”

A soldier adjusts the sighting frame.

The next shot strikes the ground beside the ward-breakers, throwing up a cloud of frozen earth. They scatter, disrupting the formation, but their magic does not entirely fail.

Vane turns towards you.

“We need to break their line before they reach the gate.”

You look across the battlefield. The beasts are moving too quickly for the garrison to rely on the ballistas alone. The ward-breakers are protected by the advancing creatures, and the fog makes it difficult to distinguish one target from another.

Then you notice something.

Every time the ward-breakers raise their staves, the violet light beneath the beasts brightens. The energy travels through the ground in narrow channels, converging beneath the creatures' spines.

The beasts are not simply animated by magic. They are being directed through a shared network of warding.

If you can disrupt the connection, their armour may become little more than dead bone.

You recognise the precise relationship between the ballista's firing angle and the distance to the advancing creatures. The adjustments you made during the preparations now become instinctive. You know how much the wind will shift a bolt, how quickly the firing arm will descend and where the projectile must strike to penetrate the creature's structure.

“Don't aim for the skull,” you tell the crew. “Its armour is thickest there. We need the spine. Between the shoulder plates, just below the upper ridge.”

The soldiers adjust the ballista.

You watch the creature's movement, waiting for it to turn broadside as it strikes the outer barricade again.

“Hold!”

The beast rears back.

“Fire!”

The bolt launches.

It strikes precisely between the obsidian plates, driving deep into the creature's spine. For a heartbeat, nothing happens.

Then the cold iron reaches the magic holding its body together.

A violent flash of white light tears through the beast. Its spine fractures, and the enormous creature collapses in a storm of bone fragments. The impact throws the ward-breakers behind it to the ground. Their violet formation flickers and dies.

A roar of approval rises from the battlements.

“One down!” Vane shouts.

The soldiers reload with renewed determination. You have shown them that the beasts can be destroyed, and that their armour is not impenetrable.

You have no time to study the creatures properly. The ballista crews are working under pressure, and the advancing beasts are already close enough to strike the gate again.

You make your decision based on what you can see.

“Target the joints!” you shout. “The armour is thickest across the skull and shoulders. Aim for the gaps where the bones meet.”

The soldiers adjust their firing angle.

The next bolt strikes the creature's front leg, tearing through the joint. It collapses onto one side, crushing a section of the barricade beneath its weight. The impact is not enough to destroy it, but the beast struggles to rise.

“Keep firing!”

A second bolt strikes its exposed ribs. Violet light bursts from the wound, and the creature's movements become erratic.

It is still alive, but it has lost its momentum.

Vane gives a grim nod.

“Good. We've slowed them. Keep the pressure on.”

The remaining siege-beasts continue towards the gate.

The second creature reaches the barricade and begins tearing at the timber with its enormous claws. The third remains further back, protected by a concentrated formation of ward-breakers.

Vane points towards the western approach.

“Shift the reserve ballista! We need to stop the second beast before it reaches the gatehouse!”

The crews move quickly, dragging the heavy weapon into position. You help guide its frame around the narrow platform, shouting instructions as the soldiers struggle against its weight.

A ward-breaker raises both hands.

The violet light above the battlefield gathers into a single point.

“Down!” Vane roars.

The magical strike hits the outer wall.

The impact sends a shockwave through the gatehouse. The ballista platform lurches, and one of the soldiers is thrown against the stone parapet. You hit the wooden boards hard, pain shooting through your shoulder.

For several seconds, the world becomes a blur of dust, shouting and falling stone.

When you look up, a section of the parapet has collapsed.

One soldier lies motionless beneath a broken beam. Another is trying to drag himself towards the stairs, blood running down his forehead. The reserve ballista has been knocked sideways, its firing mechanism damaged.

But the gate is still standing.

Below, the remaining barricades hold against the siege-beasts. The first creature lies scattered across the approach, its broken bones already beginning to fade into grey ash. The second is struggling against the reinforced timber, while the third continues to advance through the fog.

Vane pulls himself upright.

“Report!”

A soldier staggers towards him.

“The gate is holding, Commander. But the western parapet is gone. They've breached the outer warding.”

Vane looks towards the valley.

The ward-breakers are advancing again, their staves glowing brighter than before. Beyond them, more shapes are emerging from the fog. The first wave was only the beginning.

You rise unsteadily, wiping blood and dust from your face.

The garrison has survived the opening assault, but the enemy has found a weakness. The next strike may not be directed at the gate.

Vane turns towards you.

“Get off this platform! We need every defender ready for the counter-offensive.”

A fresh horn sounds from the inner courtyard.

The lower gates are still holding, but the fighting has spread beyond the wall. Somewhere beneath the battlements, the stone foundations begin to groan.

You look down towards the courtyard, where the refugee militia is waiting behind the inner barricades. If the outer gate fails, they will be the last line between the Coven and the keep.

There is no time to hesitate.

The first tremor comes before you reach the lower stairs.

It travels through the soles of your boots, a deep, grinding vibration that makes the stone beneath you seem less like a foundation and more like something alive, shifting in its sleep. Dust sifts from the ceiling. Somewhere above, the iron bells continue to toll, though their sound is muffled by several layers of stone.

The battle is already raging overhead.

You can hear it in fragments: the distant thunder of ballistas, the metallic shriek of the outer gates, the occasional roar of something enormous striking the walls. Each sound is followed by a tremor through the stairwell.

Commander Vane has given you a small squad of soldiers, four in total. They carry lanterns, short swords and the cold-iron weapons usually reserved for fighting creatures that should not exist. None of them looks particularly pleased to be descending beneath a fortress while an army attacks it from above.

“How far down?” asks the youngest soldier.

“Far enough,” you reply.

It is not a reassuring answer, but it is the only one you have.

The staircase narrows as you descend. The walls change from ordinary fortress masonry to older blocks of dark basalt, their surfaces marked with shallow carvings. Some resemble letters. Others are intricate patterns of interlocking circles and lines. You recognise the family seal from the parchment Marek showed you, though here it appears repeatedly, carved into the stone as part of a much larger design.

Your blood responds.

A faint warmth spreads through your palms. You close your fingers before the soldiers notice.

At the bottom of the staircase, a heavy iron door stands open. Its hinges have been torn from the wall, leaving deep gouges in the stone. Beyond it lies the lower vault.

The air is colder here. Not merely underground cold, but the unnatural chill of a place that has not welcomed living breath for centuries. Your lantern light stretches across a vast chamber supported by thick stone pillars. Brass conduits run between them, disappearing into the floor and walls. At the centre stands the basalt column you encountered before, its surface covered in ancient runes.

One of the soldiers approaches it.

“Is this what we're protecting?”

“Part of it.”

You move closer, studying the column. The runes are dim, but not extinguished. A faint pulse travels through them, almost too slow to see. Beneath your feet, something answers with a second vibration.

Then comes the sound.

A scrape.

A pause.

Another scrape, closer this time.

The soldier nearest the western wall raises his sword. “Something's moving.”

A section of the floor bulges.

Stone cracks. A long, skeletal limb punches through the flagstones, its joints bending in several directions at once. It is made from pale bone fused with black mineral, its surface covered in tiny runes that glow a sickly violet.

The creature drags itself into the chamber.

Then another follows.

And another.

They are not beasts in any ordinary sense. Their bodies are narrow and elongated, built for burrowing through earth and stone. Their skulls are smooth and eyeless, but each turns towards you as though it can sense the blood moving beneath your skin.

“Hold the line!” you shout.

The soldiers rush forward. Cold iron strikes bone, producing a shower of sparks. One creature twists around a soldier's blade and catches his arm in its jaws. He cries out as the violet markings crawl across his armour.

You reach for the nearest brass conduit.

The magic beneath the stone surges against your palm.

You understand, suddenly, what the creatures are doing. They are not simply attacking the vault. They are searching for something beneath it, digging towards the central foundation where the oldest wards converge.

If they reach it, the entire garrison could become unstable.

The floor shudders again.

You recognise the sound of the stone before it breaks.

The architectural braces you helped reinforce are holding. Deep beneath the chamber, iron supports groan under the pressure, but they do not give way. The original warding structure is still distributing the impact across the surrounding foundations.

You have time.

Not much, but enough.

You remember the old conduits and the way their channels meet beneath the central column. The creatures are forcing their way towards the anchor, but the braces have funnelled their approach into a narrow section of the chamber.

You look towards the soldiers.

“Fall back to the pillars. Leave the centre clear.”

One of them hesitates. “We're giving them the chamber?”

“No. We're giving them somewhere to stand.”

You move to the nearest control plate and press your palm against its surface. The runes flare beneath your fingers. With a sharp breath, you redirect the flow through the western conduit.

A deep metallic clang echoes through the vault.

The creatures continue forward.

Then the floor beneath them opens.

Ancient counterweights drop into place, and a section of the chamber's stonework shifts sideways. The creatures tumble into the narrow trench beneath it. You drive the remaining energy through the conduit, and the runes around the trench ignite.

A lattice of pale light closes over the opening.

The creatures strike against it, their limbs scraping uselessly across the glowing surface.

For the first time since entering the vault, you have the advantage.

The floor gives way beneath the central column.

A crack races through the chamber, splitting two of the ancient flagstones. One of the brass conduits tears loose, spraying sparks across the floor. The soldiers stagger as the foundations shift beneath them.

You have no time to understand the entire mechanism.

You only know that the creatures are getting closer to the column.

“Get away from the centre!” you shout.

You seize a fallen length of iron bracing and wedge it beneath the nearest conduit. The metal is painfully cold against your hands. One of the soldiers joins you, pushing his shoulder against the brace while another hacks at the creature climbing over the broken floor.

The conduit bucks.

A pulse of ancient magic runs through it and into your arms. For an instant, you see the chamber as it once was: the pillars whole, the runes bright, and figures in dark robes standing around the central column. They are not building a weapon. They are closing something.

Then the vision disappears.

You understand enough.

The conduits are not simply carrying power. They are holding the foundation together.

You press your palm against the nearest rune and allow your blood to answer it. Pain shoots through your wrist. The symbols ignite one by one, spreading along the brass channels.

“Now!” you shout.

The soldiers drive their weapons into the creatures as the floor shifts. A heavy stone slab drops across the broken section, trapping two of the horrors beneath it. The remaining creatures recoil from the sudden surge of light.

The chamber is still unstable, but the immediate breach is contained.

The silence that follows is brief.

A final creature remains, its narrow body twisted around the base of the central column. It has not attacked the soldiers. Instead, it is pressing its skull against the stone, and the violet markings across its body are pulsing in time with the ancient runes.

You approach carefully.

The creature turns its eyeless head towards you.

For one strange moment, you feel something looking back.

Not hunger. Not anger.

Recognition.

You place your hand against the column.

Your blood warms.

The creature collapses.

Its bones scatter across the floor, dissolving into grey dust. Where its body lay, a dark residue remains: a thin, shimmering substance that clings to the stone like liquid shadow.

You crouch beside it.

The residue does not behave like ordinary magic. It draws towards your fingers, then recoils, as though uncertain whether to recognise you. Beneath it, the stone bears an inscription that has been concealed beneath centuries of accumulated dust.

You brush it clean.

The words are old, but their meaning comes to you with unsettling clarity.

The first wardens did not seal the vault to imprison a creature.

They sealed it to protect something.

You look towards the central column. Its runes form a pattern around a symbol you have seen before: a broken circle, surrounded by three smaller marks. One resembles the sigil of the Bone Coven. Another resembles the silver rings worn by Balor.

The third is unmistakably your family's seal.

The Coven has not been trying to destroy the foundations.

It has been trying to reach whatever lies beneath them.

A soldier steps closer, his face pale in the lantern light.

“What does it mean?”

You look down at the residue. A faint violet thread runs through it, disappearing into a narrow crack beneath the central column.

“I don't know yet.”

It is not entirely true. You know enough to understand that the vault is more than a defensive structure. The old wardens built it around something they feared would be found. The Coven's creatures were not attempting to bring the fortress down indiscriminately. They were tunnelling towards a specific chamber.

And now they know someone has stopped them.

A distant horn sounds above.

The soldiers exchange uneasy looks.

“We should go,” one says. “The fighting won't wait.”

You nod, but before leaving, you press your palm briefly against the central column. The runes settle beneath your touch. A faint warmth passes through your hand, followed by a sensation like a door being closed somewhere far below.

The vault is sealed for now.

You have protected the foundations of Highspire, but the discovery leaves you with a more troubling question: what could the Coven possibly want badly enough to tear open the oldest wards in the valley?

The runes respond most strongly to the familiar patterns of the Coven's ancient binding magic. You recognise the structure of their work beneath the residue, and understand that someone in their ranks has been studying these foundations for a very long time. You feel a reluctant respect for the knowledge required to build such a system, even as you question what the Coven intends to do with it.

The silver pattern beneath the residue calls to something Balor awakened in you. The magic feels older than the Coven's bindings, less like a command and more like a memory. You sense that the Fae once knew what lay beneath Highspire, and that the silver rings were connected to its protection in ways you have not yet understood.

The runes remain difficult to interpret. Coven binding magic and the older silver patterns overlap beneath your hands, neither yielding easily to the other. Whatever lies below belongs to a history both factions have tried to control.

You turn towards the stairs.

The soldiers follow, carrying their wounded companion between them. Behind you, the ancient vault settles into darkness. Above, the bells continue to toll, and the fortress groans beneath the weight of the siege.

You have bought Highspire time.

Whether it will be enough is another matter.

choices.text: Rally the refugee militia in the courtyard to secure the inner keep line if the gates fail.

text.content:
The courtyard is already filling with people when you arrive.

Refugees spill from the lower passages, carrying children, blankets and whatever belongings they managed to save. Soldiers shout instructions from the wall-walk, but their voices are swallowed by the bells and the distant thunder of the siege. Beyond the outer gates, something enormous strikes the timber. The sound travels through the courtyard stones and sends a fresh wave of fear through the crowd.

You stop at the centre of the bailey.

The gates might hold for an hour. They might hold for ten minutes. You cannot afford to plan as though they will hold at all.

“Everyone listen!”

Your voice disappears beneath the noise.

A woman pushes past you, clutching a little boy against her chest. Two men argue over a cart blocking the entrance to the inner passage. Somewhere to your left, a child is crying. A soldier tries to force a line of refugees towards the cellar stairs, but the people at the back cannot see what is happening at the front. They are beginning to push.

You climb onto the stone rim of the old well.

“STOP!”

This time, your voice carries.

A few faces turn towards you. Then a few more. You raise both hands.

“Nobody moves until we know where we're going. There are enough passages for everyone, but only if we use them properly. Parents and children first. Anyone who can walk without assistance, stay where you are until you're given a group.”

The soldier beside the cellar entrance looks relieved to have someone else take responsibility.

“Where do you want them?” he asks.

“Not all into the cellars. We need clear routes between the courtyard, the infirmary and the inner keep. If the outer wall comes down, those passages become our escape routes.”

You point towards the covered arcade.

“Move the carts against the eastern wall. Keep the central path clear. Anyone with a strong back can help. Anyone carrying a child or looking after someone injured stays with them.”

The first few people obey. Others follow when they see movement.

It is not courage that makes them move. It is having something useful to do.

You jump down from the well and begin directing the volunteers. A baker's apprentice and two stable hands take charge of the carts. An elderly man who had been trying to drag a sack of flour towards the cellar is persuaded to help distribute blankets instead. You send a pair of older children to fetch water from the well, accompanied by a soldier who can keep them away from the fighting.

The courtyard begins to take shape.

Not an army, exactly. Not yet.

But a community with a purpose.

Then violet fire strikes the western side of the bailey.

It falls from above in a crooked stream, splashing across the wooden roof of a storage shed. The flames catch instantly. They burn with an unnatural brightness, turning the smoke a deep purple-grey. A volunteer drops his bucket and runs.

“Water!” someone shouts.

You grab the nearest empty pail.

“Not from the well. The fire is spreading along the roof. We need to smother it before it reaches the adjoining buildings.”

You direct two volunteers towards the sand stores while another group forms a bucket brigade. The first buckets of water hiss uselessly against the violet flames, but the sand begins to choke the fire. A soldier uses a hooked pole to pull burning roof timbers away from the neighbouring structure.

The heat presses against your face.

A section of burning wood collapses into the yard. People scatter.

“Back!” you shout. “Move back together. Don't run!”

A man stumbles and falls. The crowd behind him begins to surge.

You push through, seize his arm and pull him upright. His face is grey with fear.

“Look at me. Can you stand?”

He nods.

“Then stay with me. We need you to help the others.”

You place him beside a volunteer with a bucket and turn towards the crowd.

“There is no fire behind you. The passage is clear. Walk, don't run.”

Gradually, the panic loosens its grip.

The fire is contained before it reaches the adjoining buildings. The shed is badly damaged, but the flames are no longer spreading. You make a note of the remaining water stores and send another volunteer to check the eastern arcade for sparks.

The next problem is the wounded.

The infirmary is already crowded. A soldier with a broken leg has been laid across a table, while a young woman presses a cloth against a cut on her brother's forehead. The healer on duty looks close to exhaustion.

You move straight to the injured. There is no time for elaborate treatment, but you know how to distinguish the wounds that can wait from those that cannot. You organise the volunteers into simple tasks: clean cloths, boiled water, pressure on bleeding wounds and space around anyone struggling to breathe.

You recognise the danger of allowing the infirmary to become another place of panic. You establish a clear entrance and exit, and insist that anyone who can walk under their own strength waits in the covered arcade rather than crowding the beds.

The healer catches your eye.

“Thank you,” she says quietly.

You shake your head. “Save your strength. We'll need it.”

You notice that the infirmary's supply shelves have begun to collapse under the weight of hastily stacked equipment. You brace them with a length of timber, then organise the volunteers to move heavier supplies onto the lower shelves.

A broken stretcher is brought towards you. You repair its loose joint with a leather strap and a piece of wood, testing it before allowing the wounded soldier to be moved.

It is not grand work, but it matters. Every person who can be moved safely frees space for someone who cannot.

You recognise the importance of keeping the routes clear. The wounded cannot be carried through a crowd, and the narrow passages will become dangerous if people begin running.

You establish a simple system with the volunteers: two people carry each stretcher, one walks ahead to clear the route, and another follows to make sure nobody is left behind. You also identify the safest passage to the inner keep, away from the exposed western wall.

The system is quickly adopted. The movement of the wounded becomes calmer and more efficient.

A familiar voice calls your name.

You turn.

Kael is pushing through the crowd, his cloak torn at one shoulder and a smear of soot across his cheek. He has a short sword in one hand and a wooden shield in the other.

For a moment, the noise of the courtyard seems to recede.

“You're supposed to be keeping people alive,” he says, looking at the buckets and the injured around you.

“I am.”

“Then try not to get yourself killed doing it.”

You almost smile. “I could say the same to you.”

He looks towards the western arcade, where volunteers are still carrying supplies. Then he understands what you need without having to ask.

“Where?”

You point towards the eastern passage. “Take six people. Clear the stairwell and reinforce the inner doors. Make sure nobody gets trapped on the lower landing.”

Kael nods. “And you?”

“I'll keep the courtyard moving.”

He pauses, his expression briefly softening beneath the grime.

“Then we'll meet here.”

He does not make it sound like a promise. He makes it sound like a plan.

You watch him gather the volunteers. He speaks to them without shouting, using the same familiar certainty with which he once persuaded you to climb the old apple tree despite your better judgement. People listen. Some recognise him from Highspire; others simply recognise someone who knows what he is doing.

Together, you move through the courtyard, coordinating the evacuation and defence. When a frightened family refuses to leave their belongings behind, Kael helps them carry what they can. When two soldiers argue over where to position a barricade, you settle the disagreement before it becomes a fight.

At one point, he catches your hand as you pass.

His thumb brushes your knuckles.

“You're doing well,” he says.

There is no time to answer properly. You squeeze his hand once before letting go.

A young soldier approaches, carrying a bundle of blankets.

“Where do you want these?”

You direct him towards the infirmary, then help an exhausted woman settle her two children beneath the covered arcade. She looks up at you with frightened eyes.

“Are we going to die here?”

You crouch so that you are level with her.

“No. We're going to get you somewhere safer. Stay with the children and follow the volunteers when they come for you.”

You cannot promise that the fortress will survive. You cannot promise that every soldier will return. But you can make sure that this woman and her children are not abandoned in the confusion.

Another impact shakes the courtyard.

This one is worse.

A crack travels through the stone arch above the western entrance. Dust pours down in a thick cloud. The soldiers on the wall-walk shout, and somewhere beyond the gate a beast gives a roar that seems to vibrate inside your chest.

The outer gates are beginning to fail.

You hear the timber groan. A long, splitting sound follows, then the unmistakable crash of something striking the gate from the other side.

People freeze.

For one terrible moment, the courtyard threatens to become a stampede.

You climb onto the well again.

“LOOK AT ME!”

The nearest refugees turn. You raise your arm towards the inner keep.

“The outer gates are under attack. That is why we prepared the inner line. The children and wounded are already moving. Everyone else, take your assigned positions. Do not crowd the passages. Do not leave anyone behind.”

The instructions are repeated by the volunteers. One by one, people begin to move.

You see the results of the work you have done. The central path is clear. The infirmary has space. The water brigades are organised. The inner doors have been reinforced. Families are gathered in groups rather than scattered across the courtyard.

No one has been trampled. No child has disappeared in the confusion. No civilian has been left behind in the burning buildings.

The gates groan again.

A crack splits one of the heavy wooden beams.

The soldiers on the wall begin to fall back towards the inner keep.

You look across the courtyard. Fear remains, but it no longer controls everyone. People are helping one another. The volunteers are holding their positions. The vulnerable are behind stone rather than exposed timber.

You have not stopped the siege.

You have made sure that the people of Highspire are ready to survive it.

A horn sounds from the gatehouse. Then another, much closer.

The outer defences are collapsing.

You take your place beside the inner barricade, surrounded by the people who have chosen to stand with you.

Whatever comes through those gates will not find a helpless crowd waiting for it.

It will find a community prepared to hold the line.

choices.text: Rally the refugee militia in the courtyard to secure the inner keep line if the gates fail.

text.content:
The air above Highspire Garrison hums with a sickening, metallic static as the fog turns from ash-grey to a bruised violet.

It presses against the battlements, curling around the towers and slipping through gaps in the stonework. Every breath tastes of iron. The hairs on your arms rise as the magic gathers, and the ancient foundations beneath your feet begin to vibrate with a rhythm that is almost, but not quite, a heartbeat.

You descend from the high wall-walk, your boots skidding on the stone steps. The smouldering husk of the lead siege-beast lies collapsed in the doorway, pinning two ward-breakers beneath its obsidian armour. You bought precious minutes with the cold-iron ballistas, but the Coven's chanting outside has only grown louder.

A soldier stumbles past you, blood running from a cut above his eye. Behind him, the remaining defenders struggle to reposition the ballistas. The western parapet is broken, and violet fire flickers through the breach.

You burst out from the low archway of the subterranean stairs, cold sweat trickling down your neck. Deep below, the bedrock vault braces are holding against the tremors, but the air in the bailey smells of raw, unchannelled magic.

Your hands still tingle from touching the ancient runes. You can feel the foundations beneath you, strained but intact. Whatever the Coven is attempting, it has not yet reached the deepest chamber.

A soldier catches your arm as you emerge.

“Commander Vane wants you at the inner gate. Now.”

Behind the improvised wooden barricades in the main courtyard, the refugee militia stands four-deep. Thanks to your steadying presence, the initial panic has cleared, replaced by a tense, quiet resolve. Spear-tips glimmer in the dim light.

Mara is helping a group of children towards the cellar entrance. Tomas stands beside the barricade, gripping a borrowed spear with both hands. The volunteers look towards you as you approach, waiting for instructions.

A sharp, cracking sound cuts through the fortress.

It comes from the central gates.

For a moment, everything seems to stop. The soldiers turn. The refugees fall silent. Even the chanting beyond the walls appears to pause.

Then the iron gates buckle inward.

The first impact throws a shower of sparks across the courtyard. The second tears the central locking bar from its brackets. With a final, thunderous crash, the gates split apart and fall into the bailey.

Beyond them, the Coven's war-host stands beneath the violet fog.

The witches are arranged in concentric ranks, their staves raised towards the fortress. Between them move the remaining bone-beasts, their skeletal frames wrapped in obsidian plates. Ward-breakers crawl across the rubble, dragging their hooked tools behind them.

But the figure at the centre of the army is unlike anything else.

Tall and hooded, it wears a crown fashioned from carved spine-bones. Its robes hang in long, dark layers, marked with silver and violet symbols. In one hand it carries an ash stave, its upper end capped by a glowing soul-stone.

The soul-stone pulses.

Once.

Twice.

The ground answers.

The figure steps through the broken gates.

“People of Highspire!”

The voice does not travel through the cold air. It appears directly inside your skull, pressing against the hollow behind your ribs. Several soldiers stagger. One drops his sword and clutches his ears.

“Return what was stolen from the valley bedrock, or we will rend this keep down to the soil!”

Commander Vane steps forward.

Blood runs from the corner of his mouth. His cloak is torn, and one arm hangs awkwardly at his side, but he still holds his broadsword.

“You have no claim to this fortress,” he shouts.

The hooded figure tilts its head.

“Your fortress was built upon our inheritance. Your walls are nothing but a lid upon a grave.”

The soul-stone flashes.

A wave of force strikes the courtyard. The nearest soldiers are thrown backwards. A wooden barricade splinters, and a section of the inner wall sheds stones onto the flagstones.

You stagger, catching yourself against a pillar.

For an instant, the world becomes something else.

You see the fortress from beneath.

Its foundations stretch deep into the bedrock, surrounded by enormous channels of ancient magic. The central vault is not simply a chamber. It is part of a vast structure extending beneath the entire valley. Lines of silver and violet light cross one another, forming a pattern around something buried far below.

Something that moves.

You hear a sound like a breath drawn after centuries of silence.

Then the vision vanishes.

You are back in the courtyard, gasping.

The hooded figure has turned towards you.

Even beneath the shadow of its hood, you feel its attention settle upon your blood.

“There you are,” it says.

The words are quiet, but you hear them more clearly than the battle.

“The last living key.”

Vane moves in front of you.

“Stay behind me.”

You barely hear him.

The soul-stone pulses again, and your blood answers with a sudden flare of heat. The family seal beneath your skin seems to tighten, as though an invisible hand has closed around it.

The hooded figure raises its stave.

“Your ancestors stole the heart of the valley and buried it beneath their fortress. They made their descendants its keepers. They taught you to forget.”

It takes another step.

“Give it back.”

Vane raises his sword.

“Whatever it wants, it isn't getting it.”

The Coven ranks begin to advance. Their chanting grows louder, the voices merging into a single low note that vibrates through the stones. The remaining defenders gather around Vane, but their formation is ragged. The gates are gone. The outer courtyard is exposed. The inner keep is the only defensible position left.

You look at the hooded figure.

You think of the strange residue beneath the vault, the ancient inscription and the three symbols carved into the foundation. You think of Balor's silver rings and Marek's records. You remember that the Coven has spent centuries searching for something beneath Highspire.

Whatever it is, the leader believes you can give it to them.

And the fortress is beginning to answer.

A deep crack travels through the flagstones. Violet light shines briefly between the stones before disappearing again. The soldiers nearest you retreat instinctively.

Vane turns towards you.

“I can hold the inner courtyard for a few minutes. Perhaps longer, if the remaining ballistas can cover the breach.”

He looks towards the advancing Coven.

“But we cannot fight them here indefinitely. We need a decision.”

You understand what he is asking.

There are two ways to respond.

You could take the fight directly to the Coven leader. The soul-stone is the source of the disturbance, or at least the focus through which the leader is directing it. If you can reach the figure and disrupt the spell, the advancing army might lose its coordination. It would mean crossing the broken gates and fighting through the wardens, but hesitation could give the Coven time to complete whatever ritual it has begun.

Or you could retreat.

The inner keep contains older protections, built into the original foundations. If the ancient runes still respond to your blood, you might be able to use them to create a sealing ward. It would mean surrendering the outer courtyard and allowing the Coven to advance, but it could protect the deeper vault from whatever they are trying to awaken.

Neither choice is safe.

Behind you, the militia waits. The soldiers look towards Vane. The refugees are being moved through the inner passages, but there is still time to protect those who remain exposed.

The hooded figure raises its stave once more.

The soul-stone burns brighter.

Vane turns to you.

“Give the order.”

choices.text: Lead a sally out into the breach to cut down the Coven Leader before the spell is complete.
Fall back into the inner keep sanctum to fortify the gates and prepare a sealing ward.

text.content:
"We take the fight to them!"

Your voice cuts through the chanting. You draw your weapon and step into the open gap of the splintered gatehouse.

For half a heartbeat, nobody moves. The sight beyond the broken gates is enough to make even seasoned soldiers hesitate. The Coven's war-host stretches across the valley road, its ranks disappearing into the violet fog. Bone-beasts advance between the witches, their obsidian armour glistening with unnatural light.

Then Commander Vane lets out a fierce, roaring bark.

"Garrison! On the central mark! Cover the flank!"

The soldiers respond. Shields lock together. A handful of archers take position behind the shattered gatehouse, while the remaining defenders form around you. Vane raises his sword and charges at your side.

You run.

Cold air whips past your face, thick with the scent of ancient earth and burning iron. The ground is uneven beneath your boots, littered with broken masonry and the remains of the outer gate. Violet lightning flickers across the fog, illuminating the enemy ranks in brief, unnatural flashes.

The first ward-breaker emerges from the shadows.

It moves on elongated limbs, its narrow body hunched almost double. Iron blades protrude from its forearms, and pale runes crawl across its exposed bones. A second creature follows, then a third.

The soldiers behind you raise their shields.

"Keep moving!" Vane shouts.

You do not wait for the creatures to reach the line.

Your instinct takes over before thought can intervene. You draw your shortbow in one fluid motion, already judging the distance and the creatures' movement. The first arrow strikes the forward ward-breaker's knee. The joint buckles, sending it sprawling across the dirt.

Your second arrow finds the same weakness in the creature behind it. It collapses into the path of the others, forcing them to stumble over its broken frame.

You have not killed them, but you have taken away their speed. The soldiers surge forward, cold-iron blades flashing as they finish what you began.

You recognise the brittle stress points in their crude iron reinforcements. The creatures are built for digging, not fighting. Their frames are held together by twisted metal bands and bone joints, designed to withstand pressure from the earth rather than the impact of a weapon.

You bring your hammer down against the forward brute's main supporting rib.

The impact rings through the mist.

The iron reinforcement splits, and the creature's frame collapses beneath its own weight. You turn towards the second before it can raise its blade, striking the exposed joint where its shoulder meets its spine. The limb falls away, leaving the creature thrashing uselessly in the dirt.

You reach for the heavy flask secured at your belt. The volatile spirit inside sloshes against the glass as you pull free its stopper.

The nearest ward-breaker lunges.

You throw the flask against the threshold between the broken gates and the enemy ranks. Glass shatters. The spirit spreads across the ground, and a spark from a nearby soldier's blade catches it.

Amber flame erupts.

The sudden wall of fire scorches the animated bone and forces the creatures backwards. The soldiers use the opening to advance, forming a corridor through the smoke towards the Coven Leader.

The enemy line falters.

For the first time, the Coven's formation is disrupted. Vane sees the opening and drives his soldiers into it, his sword striking against the iron staff of a masked Warden. The two clash, sparks scattering across the road.

You keep moving.

A witch raises a stave and sends a ribbon of violet fire towards you. You throw yourself behind a broken section of gatepost. The magic strikes the stone and turns it briefly translucent, revealing a network of glowing veins beneath the surface.

The stone begins to crumble.

You roll away as the gatepost collapses, scattering fragments across the road.

"Elara!"

You turn at the sound of your name.

Kael is fighting only a few paces behind you.

His cloak is torn, and there is blood along one sleeve, but he moves with the same practical certainty you have known since childhood. He parries a swinging ward-stave, steps inside the attack and drives his shoulder into the Warden's chest. The figure stumbles backwards.

Kael finishes the movement with a sharp strike of his sword.

He glances towards you.

"You're making a habit of running towards the dangerous end of things."

"You keep following me."

"Someone has to make sure you survive your own decisions."

There is no time to answer. Another creature comes between you, and Kael moves immediately to cover your blind spot. You advance together, neither needing to explain where the other should stand.

The familiarity is almost unsettling. Even here, surrounded by violet fire and bone horrors, you know the rhythm of his movements. You know when he will turn, when he will strike and when he will leave an opening for you to use.

For a brief moment, you are not two people fighting in the ruins of a fortress. You are simply you and Kael, moving together as naturally as you once raced along the riverbank.

Then the enemy line closes again.

A soldier falls beside you, his shield arm badly wounded. You drag him behind a broken section of masonry before another ward-breaker can reach him.

"Stay down," you order.

He tries to protest.

"That wasn't a suggestion."

You take his shield and return to the fight. There are too few soldiers to waste anyone's life unnecessarily. Every person who remains standing gives someone else a chance to survive.

The Coven Leader has not moved.

The figure stands beyond the first line of wardens, its ivory mask turned towards you. The crown of carved spine-bones rises above its hood, and the soul-stone atop its ash stave pulses with increasingly violent light.

The chanting continues behind it.

You feel the magic gathering in the earth beneath your feet. It is no longer simply a disturbance in the foundations. It is being drawn upwards, pulled through the stave towards the figure's raised hand.

The hooded leader watches you approach.

"You mistake defiance for strength," it says.

The voice presses directly into your thoughts. You feel the words against the inside of your skull.

"You are a speck of dust attempting to stay a mountain."

The stave rises.

A sphere of crackling violet fire forms above the soul-stone. It grows with every heartbeat, drawing in strands of light from the witches behind the leader. The air around it bends. Loose stones lift from the ground, suspended in the pressure of the gathering magic.

Vane reaches your side.

"That thing is drawing power from the foundations," he says. "If it completes the spell, this entire courtyard could come down."

You look at the soul-stone.

The same strange residue you found beneath the vault seems to shimmer around it. You recognise the broken-circle symbol, though here it is inverted. The stone is not merely a source of power. It is a focus, directing the ancient magic towards the Coven's chosen purpose.

Your blood responds.

Heat spreads from your chest into your arms. The family seal beneath your skin pulses in time with the stone. For a moment, you sense the enormous structure beneath Highspire: the silver channels, the buried chamber and the thing waiting behind its wards.

The Coven Leader feels your recognition.

"Yes," it whispers. "You remember."

You do not.

Not properly.

But something inside you knows that the soul-stone must not be allowed to finish what it has begun.

The violet sphere expands. A soldier behind you cries out as the pressure forces him to his knees. Vane raises his sword, but even he is struggling to remain upright.

You have seconds.

The Coven Leader turns its stave towards you.

You can attempt to reach the soul-stone directly, trusting the strange magic in your blood to withstand the force surrounding it. Or you can use the fortress's remaining weapons against the leader, even if that means placing yourself directly beneath the ballista's line of fire.

You look towards the gatehouse above.

One ballista remains loaded.

Its crew are waiting for a signal.

Vane looks between you and the stave.

"Whatever you're planning, do it now!"

The soul-stone flares.

The ground splits beneath your feet.

choices.text: Drive forward and strike at the soul-stone atop the stave.
Signal the ballista crew above to fire the final cold-iron bolt onto your position.

text.content:
“Fall back to the inner arch!” you order, sweeping your arm towards the heavy stone doorway of the main keep. “We hold them at the choke point. Their numbers count for nothing if they cannot bring them to bear!”

For a moment, the soldiers hesitate. Retreat is difficult to distinguish from defeat when the enemy is already inside your walls.

Commander Vane does not hesitate.

“Move!” he roars, raising his broadsword. “Rear guard, cover the retreat! Archers, keep those staves down! Get the wounded through first!”

The courtyard erupts into movement.

You direct the remaining defenders towards the inner passage, making sure the wounded and refugees are not caught between the retreating soldiers and the advancing Coven. The militia you helped organise begins to withdraw in disciplined groups. Some carry shields, others drag makeshift barricades behind them. A few are visibly terrified, but they keep moving.

A bone-beast crashes against the broken gatehouse behind you.

Its claws scrape across the flagstones as it lurches forward, dragging a length of shattered iron behind it. A soldier turns to face it, but you seize his shoulder.

“Not here. Keep moving.”

He looks as though he wants to argue.

“We need you at the inner arch. Go!”

He obeys.

You reach the doorway just as the last of the rear guard passes through. Vane remains outside, holding the approach with three soldiers. His sword rises and falls, striking against the iron limbs of a ward-breaker.

“Commander!” you shout.

He glances towards you.

“That's an order to fall back!”

He gives a grim smile, then retreats through the arch as the final soldier clears the threshold.

“Drop the inner portcullis!”

The heavy iron grate crashes down with a deafening thud, missing the lead Coven beast by inches. Its claws strike the lower bars. Behind it, wardens hammer against the oak-and-iron barrier with staves and hooked weapons.

The sound echoes through the keep.

For a few seconds, nobody speaks.

Then the portcullis begins to tremble.

You turn towards the inner hall.

Inside the keep sanctuary, the atmosphere is suffocatingly quiet compared with the tempest outside. Shadows stretch long against the ancient stone walls, illuminated only by the dying embers of the central hearth. The air smells of smoke, sweat and old stone. Refugees huddle beside supply crates, while soldiers take positions along the narrow passage.

The sanctuary was built long before the current fortress. Its walls are thicker, its doors heavier, and its foundations descend towards the original vaults. You can feel the ancient magic beneath the floor, faint but unmistakable.

Among the huddled group of elder refugees near the hearth, you spot familiar faces looking up at you with quiet, steady faith.

Your parents are seated close together, one holding the other's hand. Their clothes are dusty, and exhaustion has drawn lines across their faces. Yet when they see you, neither panics nor rushes towards you.

Your mother simply nods.

Your father looks towards the portcullis.

“Is this where we hold them?”

You kneel beside them.

“This is where we make sure they cannot reach you.”

You cannot promise that the sanctuary will remain safe. But their presence reminds you exactly why this threshold cannot fall.

Near the supply crates, your younger sibling peers out from behind a heavy woollen cloak. Their eyes are wide, but their hands remain steady as they pass iron arrowheads to the archery squad.

They have clearly been helping for some time.

You crouch beside them.

“You should be with the others.”

“I'm helping.”

“I can see that.”

They look towards the portcullis. “Are they coming through?”

You glance at the iron bars, already beginning to glow.

“Not if we do our job.”

You take the arrowheads from them and pass the bundle to a waiting soldier. Your sibling remains close, frightened but determined. You wish you could send them somewhere beyond the reach of the fighting. There is nowhere left.

In the quiet of the inner hall, you stand at the front line, unburdened by immediate family to protect and completely focused on the iron latch before you.

The others look towards you for instructions. Their fear is real, but so is their willingness to follow.

You study the doorway, the narrow approach and the old carvings around the frame. There is no room for a large force to advance together. If the portcullis fails, the Coven will have to enter through a narrow passage, where a handful of defenders can hold them.

You have no intention of making it easy.

A sudden flash illuminates the hall.

Outside, the iron portcullis begins to glow red hot as Coven magic bleeds through the seams. The metal bends inwards, its lower edge glowing like a forge. A soldier throws a bucket of water against it. Steam explodes across the doorway, forcing everyone nearby to retreat.

“Back!” Vane orders.

The portcullis groans.

A hooked limb reaches through the widening gap, scraping against the stone floor. The soldiers raise their shields. An archer looses an arrow, but it glances off the creature's armour.

Vane wipes sweat from his brow.

“The iron will not hold forever.”

He looks towards the sanctuary walls.

“What is our move?”

You examine the ancient carvings around the doorway. Their patterns are similar to those in the lower vaults. The same interlocking circles, the same broken symbol surrounded by smaller marks. The fortress was not built simply to defend the valley. Its oldest structures were designed to contain and regulate the magic beneath it.

The Coven knows this.

The hooded leader's demand echoes in your mind.

Return what was stolen from the valley bedrock.

You think of the soul-stone, the buried chamber and the strange residue left behind by the ward-breakers. You still do not understand what the Coven is trying to recover, but you know that the sanctuary is connected to it.

There may be a way to use that connection.

Deep below, the vault anchor remains intact. If you can reach its power through the old conduits, you might be able to send a pulse through the keep walls. It could disrupt the Coven's magic, perhaps even force the creatures away from the gates.

But the attempt would be dangerous. The anchor was built to contain something, not to be used as a weapon. Directing its power without understanding the consequences could weaken the very foundations you are trying to protect.

The alternative is more immediate.

You could organise a shield wall at the threshold, using the narrow passage to prevent the Coven from overwhelming the defenders. The wounded and refugees would be moved deeper into the sanctuary while the soldiers held each doorway in turn.

It would be a brutal defence, fought room by room.

But it would keep the enemy away from the people behind you.

Kael steps beside you, tightening the strap around his shield.

He has been helping the wounded and organising the volunteers since the retreat began. There is a fresh cut along his cheek, but he seems barely aware of it.

“You've got that look again,” he says.

“What look?”

“The one you get when you've found three ways for something to go wrong and you're trying to choose the least terrible.”

You glance towards the glowing portcullis.

“I need you to help move the refugees towards the rear chambers. Keep the passage clear and make sure nobody gets separated.”

He studies your face.

“And you?”

“I'll decide how we hold the line.”

Kael looks as though he wants to argue. Instead, he places his hand briefly against your arm.

“Whatever you choose, don't make yourself the only person standing between them and the enemy.”

There is something in his voice that makes you pause. He is not asking you to abandon the fight. He is reminding you that the people around you are capable of sharing its weight.

“I won't,” you say.

He holds your gaze for another moment, then turns to carry out your instructions.

Vane watches you study the carvings.

“You have seen these before,” he says.

“In the lower vaults.”

“Can they help us?”

You look towards the portcullis.

“I think so. But I need to decide how much risk we're willing to take.”

Vane nods once.

“Then decide quickly. I can give you a few minutes, no more.”

Another impact shakes the sanctuary.

The portcullis bows inwards. One of its upper brackets tears free from the wall and crashes onto the flagstones. A soldier is knocked aside by the falling metal. Two others drag him clear.

The Coven's chanting rises outside.

You feel the ancient magic beneath the sanctuary responding. The carvings around the doorway glow faintly, as though they recognise the pressure building against them. Your blood warms in answer.

There is no time left for hesitation.

You turn towards the defenders.

“Listen carefully. We have two choices. Neither guarantees our survival, but we are not going to let the Coven reach the foundations without a fight.”

The portcullis groans again.

You raise your hand.

“Prepare yourselves.”

choices.text: Use the subterranean vault anchor to discharge a magical pulse back through the keep wall.
Form a shield wall at the threshold and prepare for a room-by-room defense.

text.content:
You do not slow your stride.

The Coven Leader stands beyond the shattered gates, its ash stave raised above the battlefield. The violet sphere at its tip has grown so bright that the surrounding fog appears almost black. Threads of energy stretch from the stone towards the witches behind it, each pulse drawing more power from the foundations beneath Highspire.

You run directly towards it.

A ward-breaker lunges from your left. Its iron blade catches the edge of your clothing, tearing through the fabric, but you twist away before it can reach your skin. You leap over its collapsing frame and drive your weight towards the glowing stave.

The Coven Leader turns.

For the first time, its composure falters.

“You cannot—”

The words disappear beneath the roar of gathering magic.

The violet orb flares blindingly.

Raw, unrefined power surges through the air, catching you in the chest like a physical blow. Your feet leave the ground. The static burns across your skin, setting every nerve alight. You feel something inside your blood answer the force, not resisting it but recognising it.

The impact should throw you backwards.

Instead, you keep moving.

You recognise the volatile energetic bleed for what it is: an unstable balance of vital and necrotic force. The magic is trying to overwhelm your body by attacking everything at once, but you understand how to manage the shock.

You turn your shoulders and draw the force away from your chest, allowing it to spread across your back and arms rather than striking your heart and lungs directly. Pain tears through your muscles. Your hands shake, and your vision blurs, but you remain conscious.

You have treated people whose bodies were close to failing. You know that survival sometimes means controlling the damage rather than pretending it can be avoided.

You use that knowledge now.

You see the weakness before the magic strikes.

The soul-stone is held in an iron socket at the top of the stave. The metal has been twisted by the strain of containing so much power, and a hairline fracture runs through the joint where the stone meets the carved wood.

It is a structural failure waiting to happen.

You adjust your grip and bring your weapon towards the precise point where the iron socket meets the stave. There is no time for a second attempt. You strike with everything you have, aiming not at the stone itself but at the fragile structure holding it in place.

Your instincts take over.

The violet fire arcs towards you, splitting into three twisting streams. You twist in mid-air, narrowly avoiding the first. The second catches your shoulder and sends a flash of pain down your arm. You use the momentum to turn your body and bring the butt of your weapon down in a punishing arc.

You have hunted creatures that moved faster than thought. You have learned to read the instant before an attack, the shift of weight and the direction of a strike.

The Coven Leader is powerful, but it is still holding a weapon.

And weapons can be broken.

Your strike lands.

CRACK.

The sound is unlike anything you have heard before. It seems to come from the stone itself, from beneath the battlefield and from somewhere impossibly far away.

The soul-stone splits.

For an instant, a thin line of white light runs through its centre. Then the entire crystal bursts into a shower of crystalline sparks.

The violet sphere collapses.

A high-pitched screech tears through the fog as the Coven magic backfires. The witches behind the leader stagger, their staves erupting in showers of sparks. Several fall to their knees, clutching their heads. The chanting stops abruptly, leaving a silence so sudden that you can hear the fragments of the soul-stone striking the flagstones.

Across the battlefield, the animated bone-beasts collapse.

Their limbs fold beneath them. Obsidian armour crashes to the ground, and the runes that animated their bodies fade into dull grey marks. The ward-breakers fall apart, their iron reinforcements scattering across the road.

The entire Coven formation breaks.

You land heavily on the flagstones.

For several seconds, you cannot move. Your chest burns, and your hands feel as though they have been plunged into boiling water. The air is thick with the smell of scorched stone and something older, something like a forest floor disturbed after centuries beneath the earth.

The Coven Leader staggers backwards.

Its ash stave is broken, the upper half hanging from a twisted length of iron. One gloved hand reaches towards the ruined mask covering its face.

“No,” it whispers.

The voice is no longer inside your head. It is small, strained and unmistakably human.

The mask cracks.

Beneath it, you glimpse a face, though the features are blurred by the violet light gathering around the figure. The leader looks towards the broken soul-stone, then towards you.

“You have no idea what you have done.”

You try to stand.

“What were you trying to release?”

The figure recoils as though the question itself has wounded it.

“Release?” it repeats. “We were trying to reclaim what was taken.”

The ground trembles.

The fragments of the soul-stone lift from the flagstones, suspended in the air around the leader. They begin to dissolve into the mist, and the figure's outline follows them. Its robes unravel into strands of violet smoke.

You reach towards it.

“Tell me what is beneath the vault!”

For a moment, the hooded figure looks directly at you.

Then its voice returns, quieter than before.

“Ask your ancestors what they buried.”

The figure disappears.

The mist closes over the space where it stood.

You remain on one knee, staring at the empty ground.

The battle has ended, but the words leave you with no sense of victory.

Your ancestors buried something beneath Highspire. The Coven has spent generations trying to reach it. The soul-stone was a key to their attempt, but destroying it has not answered the question of what lies below.

A deep pulse moves through the bedrock.

You feel it in your hands.

The magic beneath the fortress is still there.

It is no longer being drawn upwards through the Coven's stave, but something has changed. The ancient channels beneath the battlefield are glowing faintly, and the family seal beneath your skin responds with a warmth that is almost painful.

You look towards the keep.

The old walls stand. The gates are broken, the courtyard is damaged, and smoke rises from the battlements. But the fortress has not fallen.

A soldier approaches, leaning heavily on his sword.

“Is it over?”

You look towards the collapsed bone-beasts and the retreating figures of the surviving witches.

“The attack is over.”

He follows your gaze.

“What about the Coven?”

“They're not finished.”

He looks at you, waiting for more.

You have no answer that would make him feel better.

A horn sounds from the gatehouse. This time it is not an alarm, but a signal calling the surviving defenders together. Commander Vane appears through the smoke, supported by two soldiers. His face is streaked with blood and soot, and his sword is chipped along one edge.

He looks at the ruined stave.

Then at you.

“You broke their spell.”

“I broke their focus.”

“Whatever you call it, the beasts are down and their formation has scattered.”

Vane surveys the battlefield. Soldiers begin emerging from the keep, some carrying wounded companions, others helping refugees from the inner passages. The surviving militia cautiously approaches the broken gates.

Kael pushes through the gathering defenders.

His face is pale beneath the soot, and one sleeve is dark with blood. When he reaches you, he stops as though checking that you are really standing there.

“You look terrible,” he says.

You manage a tired breath that might almost be a laugh.

“You should see the other one.”

He looks towards the scattered remains of the soul-stone.

“I think I already have.”

For a moment, neither of you speaks. Then he reaches for your hand, careful of the burns across your skin.

“You came back,” he says.

You close your fingers around his.

“So did you.”

He holds on for a little longer before turning to help the wounded.

The first pale light of dawn begins to filter through the thinning fog.

Highspire has survived the siege.

But beneath the fortress, the ancient foundations continue to pulse. Somewhere below, beyond the sealed chambers and forgotten passages, something has heard the destruction of the soul-stone.

You can feel it waiting.

For now, there are people to find, wounded to help and defenders to gather. The living must come before the mysteries of the dead.

You push yourself upright.

“Bring everyone to the courtyard,” you tell Vane. “We count our survivors, treat the wounded and secure the keep. Then we find out what the Coven was really trying to recover.”

Vane nods.

Around you, the surviving defenders begin to move.

The siege is over.

The consequences are only beginning.

choices.text: Survey the aftermath and gather the surviving defenders.

text.content:
You do not rush towards the Coven Leader.

The violet magic gathering around the soul-stone is too powerful to meet directly. Every pulse sends a tremor through the ground, and the air above the battlefield twists with heatless fire. The surviving defenders are scattered across the courtyard, many struggling to hold their positions. A few have begun retreating towards the inner keep.

You look towards the gatehouse.

The old ballistas stand along the upper battlements, their great wooden frames reinforced with iron brackets. Their crews have been working throughout the siege, but the weapons are difficult to aim in the shifting fog. You remember the preparations, the arguments over their calibration and the weight of the cold-iron bolts.

You need one clean shot.

Perhaps three.

You raise your arm high and whistle.

The sound cuts through the battlefield, sharp and piercing. It is the signal you agreed upon with Vane: a call to abandon the current firing pattern and concentrate every available weapon on a single target.

For a moment, nothing happens.

Then a figure appears above the gatehouse parapet.

Commander Vane.

He catches your gesture and immediately understands.

“BALLISTAS! TARGET THE STAVE!”

One of the crews turns its weapon. Another follows, its heavy frame groaning as the mechanism shifts. You can see the soldiers struggling with the cranks, their movements hurried but controlled.

The Coven Leader notices.

Its hood turns towards the battlements.

The soul-stone brightens.

“NO!”

The voice strikes the inside of your skull. A wave of violet energy rolls across the battlefield, throwing two soldiers from their feet. The nearest ballista shudders as its iron fittings glow red.

Vane does not retreat.

“DEPRESS CRANK! FIRE ON MY MARK!”

You realise the Coven Leader is preparing to strike the gatehouse. If the spell reaches the battlements, the crews will never get their shot.

You sprint towards the centre of the courtyard, drawing the leader's attention away from the weapons above. The ground is littered with broken shields, splintered timber and the remains of the bone-beasts. You leap over a fallen soldier and reach the shattered remains of a stone pillar.

The Coven Leader raises its stave.

The violet orb flares.

You dive behind the pillar.

“MARK!”

The air above splits open with a deafening screech.

Three heavy, quicksilver-tipped cold-iron bolts rain down from the battlements like lightning strikes, plunging through the fog.

The first hits the earth between you and the Coven Leader.

The impact throws dirt and stone into the air. The shockwave slams against your back, driving you hard into the ground. Your ears ring, and for a moment the world becomes a blur of grey dust and violet light.

The second bolt strikes the stave.

The third strikes the Coven Leader directly in the chest.

A terrible metallic shriek tears across the courtyard.

The cold iron pierces the dark figure's robes, pinning it against the cobbled road outside the gates. The soul-stone at the stave's tip pulses once, twice, then begins to fracture. Quicksilver spreads across its surface in branching lines, swallowing the violet light.

The Coven Leader struggles.

Its free hand claws at the ground. The robes writhe around the bolts, trying to pull the figure upright, but the cold iron holds it fast.

The magic collapses.

A shockwave rolls outwards, nullifying the violet fire instantly. Every remaining flame gutters and dies. The runes on the bone-beasts fade, and their bodies fall apart in great clattering heaps of marrow, stone and iron.

The ward-breakers drop their weapons.

Across the battlefield, the surviving Coven soldiers look towards their fallen leader. Some attempt to raise their staves, but the magic that sustained their formation has vanished. Others retreat towards the woods, abandoning their wounded and leaving their weapons scattered across the road.

The frontline is broken.

For several seconds, nobody moves.

Then the Coven Leader lifts its head.

Beneath the torn hood, you glimpse the pale outline of a face. The figure looks towards you, and despite the bolts holding it to the ground, you feel the weight of its attention.

“You have broken nothing,” it says.

Its voice is weaker now, stripped of the power that carried it across the battlefield.

You rise slowly from behind the pillar.

“What were you trying to release?”

The figure gives a low, rasping laugh.

“Release? You still think this was about imprisonment?”

A tremor passes beneath your feet.

The stones of the courtyard shift. Far below, something answers the disturbance with a slow, heavy pulse. The family seal beneath your skin warms, and the magic in your blood responds before you can stop it.

The Coven Leader notices.

“Ask your ancestors,” it whispers. “Ask them what they buried beneath your feet.”

Before you can move closer, the remaining violet energy around the figure begins to unravel. Its robes dissolve into strands of ash, and the face beneath the hood disappears into the fog.

The cold-iron bolts remain embedded in the road.

The Coven Leader is gone.

You stare at the place where it stood.

The siege has ended, but its final words leave a question that seems more dangerous than anything that came before.

What did your ancestors bury?

A shout draws your attention back to the gatehouse.

“Clear the courtyard!”

Commander Vane is descending the steps, one hand pressed against a wound in his side. His face is pale, but he remains upright. Behind him, the ballista crews are already securing their weapons and checking the condition of the upper walls.

He reaches you and looks towards the broken stave.

“Three bolts,” he says. “I thought we would be limited to one.”

“You landed all three.”

“Because you gave us a target.”

He looks over the battlefield, taking in the fallen creatures and the retreating Coven soldiers.

“That signal may have saved everyone still standing.”

You glance towards the gatehouse. The ballistas have done their work, but the walls are damaged, and several sections of the parapet have collapsed. The defenders will need to secure the perimeter before the Coven can regroup.

A familiar figure emerges through the drifting dust.

Kael reaches you, his expression caught somewhere between relief and disbelief. He looks at the broken pillar, then at the three bolts embedded in the road.

“Vane's aim was good,” he says, offering you a firm hand to pull you up from the dust, “but your call was better.”

You take his hand.

“I was hoping someone would hear me.”

“Half the garrison heard you. The other half probably felt the whistle in their teeth.”

You almost smile, but the pain in your chest makes it difficult. Kael notices the way you are holding yourself and looks towards your shoulder.

“Are you hurt?”

“Nothing that needs attention before everyone else.”

“That isn't what I asked.”

His voice is quiet, but there is no room for argument in it. He steadies you for a moment before releasing your hand.

The courtyard begins to stir.

A cheer rises from the surviving militia. It is not the roar of a victorious army. It is ragged, exhausted and interrupted by coughing and the cries of the wounded. But it grows as soldiers recognise that the bone-beasts are no longer moving and the violet fire has disappeared.

Mara emerges from behind a broken wagon, helping Elsie across the courtyard. Tomas follows with a group of villagers carrying wounded defenders on makeshift stretchers.

You see people who were baking bread, repairing carts and tending gardens only yesterday. Now they are covered in ash, carrying weapons and searching the rubble for their neighbours.

They have survived.

That matters more than any cheer.

Vane raises his voice.

“Defenders! Secure the gates. Search the fallen for survivors, but do not approach the Coven's remaining weapons without a warding officer. Scouts to the tree line. Nobody leaves the perimeter alone.”

He turns towards you.

“You called the shot. You should lead the first sweep.”

You look beyond the broken gates, where the retreating Coven soldiers have vanished into the dark woods. The fog is thinning, but the mountains remain hidden. Somewhere beneath the fortress, the ancient magic continues to pulse.

You have won the battle.

You have not yet secured the valley.

choices.text: Lead the garrison out to secure the perimeter.

text.content:
The inner keep shudders around you.

Dust falls from the vaulted ceiling as another impact strikes the heavy oak doors. The iron bands across their surface glow red, and the timber groans beneath the pressure. Beyond them, the Coven's forces continue their assault, hammering against the entrance with something large enough to shake the foundations.

Commander Vane stands near the threshold, directing the remaining soldiers into position. Their shields are raised, but you can see the strain in their arms. The defenders have already fought through the night. They cannot hold the doors indefinitely.

You look towards the central pillar.

Beneath the sanctuary floor, the ancient foundation anchor waits. You remember the subterranean chamber, the brass conduits and the pulse of power that ran through the stone. Your ancestors built this fortress around something far older than its walls. The keep is not merely a military stronghold. Its foundations are part of the original binding.

And you know how to reach it.

“Cover me!” you shout to Vane. “I'm routing the foundation anchor back through the keep walls!”

He turns towards you.

“How long?”

“I don't know.”

“Then make it quick.”

Vane signals two soldiers to take position beside the pillar. They raise their shields as another blow lands against the doors. The iron fittings scream, and a narrow crack appears along the timber.

You sprint across the sanctuary.

The central pillar rises from the floor like a column of blackened stone. Its surface is marked with shallow carvings, many worn almost smooth by centuries of use. You recognise the family seal among them. It is the same symbol you saw beneath the garrison, carved into the ancient vault anchor.

You place both hands flat against the cold stone.

At first, nothing happens.

Then you feel it.

A deep vibration travels through your palms, up your arms and into your chest. The bedrock hums beneath you, carrying a pulse of magic that seems to stretch beyond the keep, through the foundations and into the hills surrounding Highspire.

The anchor is still functioning.

The Coven has been attacking the walls, but the power beneath them has not been destroyed. It has simply been left dormant, waiting for someone with the right blood to awaken it.

You close your eyes.

The first sensation is cold. Then pressure. Then an awareness of countless channels running beneath the fortress, branching through stone and earth like the roots of an enormous tree.

You reach into the flow.

The magic responds immediately.

It rises through your hands, filling your arms with a force that is almost unbearable. The runes beneath your palms begin to glow, and thin lines of white light spread across the pillar.

You try to direct the current towards the walls.

The energy resists.

It is too much to control by force alone. You feel the old channels pulling in different directions, each carrying a separate part of the fortress's protective structure. The gatehouse, the inner arches, the foundation anchor. All of them are connected, but the flow has been disrupted by the Coven's assault.

You remember the hidden pattern beneath the vaults.

The channels were not designed to be opened individually. They were meant to work together.

You change your approach, allowing the current to move through the network rather than forcing it through a single path. The magic spreads from the central pillar into the walls, finding the ancient defensive runes built into the stone.

One by one, they awaken.

White light races along the floor.

The soldiers nearest the pillar stumble backwards as the energy passes beneath their feet. Vane turns, shielding his eyes.

“Whatever you're doing,” he calls, “it's working!”

Another impact strikes the doors.

The iron bands flare brighter, and the wood begins to split.

You feel the strain in your shoulders. The current is growing stronger, and the anchor is drawing more power from the bedrock than you intended. You could release it now, but the defensive runes have not yet reached the threshold.

If you stop too soon, the energy will collapse before it reaches the entrance.

You hold on.

Across the room, your parents stand together near the inner wall. Your mother has one hand pressed against your father's arm, while his lips move in a quiet prayer.

They have watched you face things no parent should ever have to witness. They have seen the village burn, the garrison threatened and the world you knew become something unrecognisable.

Now they watch the runes along the walls ignite with brilliant white light.

Your mother's eyes meet yours.

She does not call for you to stop. She does not ask whether you are frightened. She simply holds your father's hand and continues to pray.

Their quiet words seem to merge with the hum of the stone.

For a brief moment, the pressure eases. You feel the familiar weight of their presence behind you, a reminder of the people whose lives you are trying to protect.

Your younger sibling stands behind the soldiers, one arm raised to shield their eyes from the growing glare.

The fear that has been written across their face since the destruction of Highspire begins to give way to something else.

Awe.
