They stare at the glowing runes as the light spreads across the walls, following the old carvings towards the entrance.

You catch their expression through the brightness.

They are seeing you do something they cannot yet understand. Perhaps they will ask about it later. Perhaps there will be time to explain that you were frightened too, that you had no certainty the magic would obey you.

For now, you keep your hands against the stone.

There is nobody beside you.

The soldiers are holding the entrance, and Vane is shouting orders behind you, but the pillar has become the centre of your world.

You stand alone at its base, holding the full weight of the keep's power in your bare hands.

The light grows until the sanctuary disappears behind it. You can no longer see the walls or the faces of the defenders. There is only the stone beneath your palms and the ancient current moving through your blood.

You understand, with sudden clarity, that the fortress was never intended to depend on a single person.

Your ancestors built a system that could outlast them.

You are simply the one who has remembered how to use it.

The final defensive rune ignites.

A deep metallic note rolls through the keep.

You open your eyes.

“Vane! Get everyone away from the doors!”

He hears the urgency in your voice and immediately orders the soldiers to fall back. They retreat towards the inner passage, dragging the wounded with them.

The oak doors buckle.

A final blow lands from outside.

The timber begins to split.

You release the current.

The foundation anchor answers.

A massive concussive wave of white force detonates outward from the threshold.

The doors shake violently in their frames. The iron portcullis, glowing red from the Coven's sustained assault, cools instantly. Its surface turns dark, and the molten-looking runes etched across it disappear.

The wave continues beyond the entrance.

You hear the Coven's siege machinery collapse. Something heavy strikes the ground outside, followed by a series of sharp cracks as the remaining magical restraints fail. The rhythmic battering against the wood ceases entirely.

Silence follows.

Not the tense silence of a battlefield waiting for another attack, but something deeper. The sudden absence of the Coven's magic leaves the air feeling strangely empty.

The defensive runes remain lit.

Their white glow spreads across the walls, holding the entrance secure. Beyond the doors, you hear scattered cries and the retreating footsteps of soldiers who have lost the power sustaining their assault.

The magic forced through the foundation has purged the Coven's siege force from the threshold.

You slowly lift your hands from the pillar.

Your fingers tremble.

The stone is no longer cold. Beneath your palms, it carries a gentle warmth, like something living that has finally been allowed to rest. The runes begin to dim, fading from brilliant white to a faint silver glow.

You stagger backwards.

Vane reaches you before you fall.

“Easy.”

He catches your arm and steadies you. His expression is difficult to read beneath the soot and blood.

“Is it finished?”

You look towards the doors.

“I think the assault is.”

He studies the fading runes.

“And the anchor?”

You glance down at your hands. Thin traces of white light remain beneath your skin, fading with each breath.

“Still there. I haven't destroyed it.”

“Good. I would rather not discover what happens if the foundations of this place decide to move.”

Despite your exhaustion, you almost smile.

Around you, the surviving defenders begin to emerge from their positions. Some check the doors, while others help the wounded towards the sanctuary's inner chambers. The immediate danger has passed, but nobody is ready to celebrate.

You look at the ancient carvings on the pillar.

The Coven wanted something beneath Highspire. Its leader spoke of reclaiming what had been taken, and the soul-stone was only a means of reaching it. Your ancestors did not build the vaults simply to imprison a source of power.

There is still a truth buried beneath the fortress.

And now you have awakened the very magic that was meant to keep it hidden.

Vane follows your gaze.

“Whatever comes next,” he says, “we face it with the keep standing.”

You nod, though you know the walls are not the only thing that needs protecting.

For now, the people outside need to know whether they are safe. The wounded need attention, and the defenders need to see the aftermath with their own eyes.

You take one last look at the pillar before turning towards the entrance.

choices.text: Step out through the unbarred doors to inspect the quiet hall.

text.content:
“Form the line!” you roar, stepping to the very front of the archway with your weapon drawn. “Not one step back!”

The order carries through the inner hall, cutting across the groans of the wounded and the thunder of the siege outside. For a moment, the defenders hesitate. They are exhausted, frightened and painfully aware that the doors behind them are the final barrier between the Coven and the heart of Highspire.

Then Commander Vane moves.

“SHIELDS FORWARD! CLOSE THE GAPS!”

The remaining garrison guards rush into position beside you. Metal strikes metal as their shields lock together, overlapping across the narrow entrance. You hear the scrape of boots against stone, the uneven breathing of men and women who have already fought longer than they thought possible.

There are fewer defenders than there should be.

Some lie wounded in the sanctuary. Others have fallen on the battlements or disappeared beneath the rubble outside. The militia who helped hold the lower courtyard have been driven back into the keep, and the refugees are gathered behind the inner arches.

You look over your shoulder.

They are watching you.

Mara has Elsie close against her side. Tomas is helping an injured soldier sit upright. Several villagers have taken up whatever weapons they could find, but none of them looks ready for another charge.

You turn back towards the entrance.

They do not need to see your fear.

They need to see that the line is holding.

The portcullis shudders.

A heavy impact strikes it from outside, followed by another. The iron bars bend towards you, their edges glowing red from the Coven's magic. The oak doors split along their central seam, sending splinters skittering across the floor.

Vane steps beside you.

“Whatever comes through, we keep them in the doorway.”

You nod.

The archway is narrow. The Coven may have greater numbers, but it cannot bring them all through at once. The ruined entrance has become a choke point, and you intend to make every inch of it costly.

The final blow lands.

The iron portcullis buckles outward. The red-glowing timber splits apart, and the doors collapse inwards with a crash that shakes dust from the ceiling.

Beyond them, the Coven's vanguard surges into the gap.

The first attackers are armoured in bone plates, their faces hidden behind pale masks. They carry heavy clubs and hooked blades, moving with the unnatural coordination of soldiers whose movements are being controlled by the same spell.

Behind them, more figures gather in the fog.

“Hold!” Vane shouts.

The first impact hits your shield.

The force drives you backwards half a step. The guard beside you grunts as another club crashes against his armour. A second attacker tries to force its way around the edge of the formation, but there is nowhere to go. The stone walls prevent the Coven from surrounding you.

You strike back.

You fight with deadly efficiency in the tight space.

There is no room for broad swings, so you keep your movements short and controlled. You watch the attackers' shoulders, waiting for the instant before they commit to a strike. Their heavy clubs are dangerous, but slow. Every time one rises, you slip inside its reach.

Your blade finds the gaps between their bone armour: beneath the ribs, behind the elbow, at the narrow joint where shoulder meets neck.

One attacker collapses against the shield wall. Another loses its grip on its weapon and falls beneath the press of the others.

You have hunted creatures in cramped woodland and narrow ravines. You know that a confined space can be more useful than a wide battlefield, provided you understand where your enemy cannot move.

Here, the Coven cannot bring its numbers to bear.

You make every opening count.

The heavy iron shield you fortified takes the brunt of the attack.

You planted its reinforced edge against the stone before the charge began, and now the additional ironwork proves its worth. Each blow sends a vibration through your arms, but the shield holds.

You angle it slightly, allowing the force of an attack to slide sideways rather than strike directly. The attacker loses its balance, exposing its flank to the guard beside you.

“Now!” you shout.

The guard drives a spear through the opening.

You shift your weight and absorb the next blow, turning the attack away from the soldier on your other side. The formation begins to work as a single mechanism: one shield receives the impact, another redirects it, and the weapons behind them strike whenever the Coven loses its footing.

You know how to make something withstand pressure.

The shield wall is no different.

You move between the wounded and the frontline, keeping the defensive wall intact.

A guard takes a heavy blow to the ribs and collapses against the shield beside him. You catch his shoulder before he falls completely, pulling him backwards while another soldier steps into the gap.

His breathing is shallow, but he is alive.

You press a hand against his side, feeling the damage beneath his armour. There is no time for proper treatment, only enough to steady him and prevent him from bleeding further.

Then you return to the line.

A second defender falls. You take their place, raising your weapon against the next attacker. You are not the strongest person in the formation, but you know how to recognise when someone is about to fail and where you are needed most.

Every gap matters.

Every fallen defender leaves another person exposed.

You move wherever the line threatens to break, helping the wounded retreat and stepping forward whenever another shield drops.

The first wave crashes against you.

The second follows before the first has fully fallen.

For ten grueling minutes, the threshold becomes an unyielding wall of steel, bone and iron will.

The noise is almost impossible to separate into individual sounds. Clubs strike shields. Blades scrape against armour. Soldiers shout orders, warnings and names. The Coven attackers press forward, but the narrow doorway prevents them from bringing their full strength against you.

Vane holds the centre.

You remain near the front, watching for weaknesses in the formation. Every time the line begins to bend, you call for the nearest defenders to close ranks. When an attacker tries to climb over the fallen bodies at the threshold, the soldiers behind you drag it down before it can reach the sanctuary.

The floor becomes slippery with mud, ash and blood.

Your arms begin to shake.

A guard beside you loses his footing, and the entire line shifts. For one terrible moment, the Coven gains ground. A bone-armoured figure forces its shoulder between two shields, pushing them apart.

“Close it!” you shout.

Vane throws his weight against the gap. You drive your weapon into the attacker, and the guard on the other side regains his footing. The shields lock together again.

The line holds.

A few paces behind you, someone begins calling the names of the wounded. The voices are familiar. Villagers, soldiers and refugees are all working together now, passing water, dragging the injured away from the entrance and bringing fresh weapons to those still standing.

You hear Mara calling for bandages.

Tomas shouts that the eastern passage is clear.

The keep is no longer a collection of frightened people waiting to be rescued. It is a community defending the place where they have found shelter.

Through the press of defenders, you catch sight of your companion.

Kael is fighting just behind the front line, keeping the attackers from reaching the wounded. His face is streaked with soot, and his movements are becoming slower, but he refuses to leave his position.

For a moment, your eyes meet.

He gives you a brief, determined nod.

You remember the two of you as children, racing along the riverbank and arguing over who had won. Back then, the worst consequence of losing had been a bruised knee or a stolen pastry.

Now he is standing in a broken fortress, holding a line beside you while the world seems to be coming apart.

You turn back towards the attackers.

There will be time to speak to him if you both survive.

The pressure begins to change.

The attackers are no longer advancing with the same coordination. Their movements become erratic, and the violet light beneath their armour flickers. Several look towards the woods behind them, where distant horns are sounding.

Vane notices it too.

“They're losing their command!”

You look beyond the fallen vanguard.

The Coven's magic is weakening. Whatever has been sustaining the assault is failing, and the creatures at the front are beginning to retreat rather than press forward.

One of them raises its club for another strike, then hesitates.

You step towards it.

It backs away.

The figure behind it turns and disappears into the fog. A moment later, the rest begin to follow. The remaining invaders abandon the breach, dragging their wounded and leaving broken weapons scattered across the stones.

Nobody pursues them.

The defenders are too exhausted, and the threat beyond the gates has not yet been fully understood.

Instead, you hold the line until the last attacker has disappeared.

Then you lower your weapon.

The silence is almost painful.

Your arms tremble, and your breathing comes in short, ragged gasps. The sanctuary is filled with the smell of smoke, sweat and blood. Morning light begins to stream through the broken doorway, illuminating the wreckage outside.

Vane rests one hand against the wall.

“Nobody follows them,” he orders. “Secure the entrance. Check the wounded. We hold this position until the perimeter is clear.”

He turns towards you.

“You kept them out.”

You look at the broken portcullis and the bodies scattered across the threshold.

“We kept them out.”

Vane gives a tired nod.

Around you, the surviving defenders begin to lower their shields. Some embrace one another. Others sit down where they stand, unable to keep their legs beneath them any longer.

Behind the line, Mara reaches Elsie and draws her into a tight embrace. Tomas helps a wounded guard towards the sanctuary benches. The refugees begin emerging from the inner passages, looking towards the broken entrance as though they cannot quite believe the fighting has stopped.

Highspire has survived.

Not because its walls were unbreakable, or because its soldiers were stronger than the Coven.

It survived because people who had every reason to run chose to stand beside one another.

You look towards the pale morning sky beyond the ruined doorway.

The siege is over, but the Coven Leader's words remain with you. Something lies beneath the fortress, something your ancestors buried and the Coven has spent generations trying to reclaim.

For now, you put that thought aside.

The living need your attention first.

text.content:
The ash-grey fog finally lifts, cut through by the sharp, pale gold of an autumn sunrise.

For the first time since the destruction of Highspire, you can see the mountains beyond the valley clearly. Their peaks are touched with early light, though dark stains of smoke still drift above the forest. The morning should feel peaceful. Instead, the brightness seems almost unfamiliar after so many hours of fire and darkness.

Highspire Garrison is silent now, save for the crackle of dying fires and the heavy, rhythmic thud of soldiers clearing debris from the courtyard. The air smells of pine smoke, wet stone and the lingering scent of dissipated magic.

The siege has ended.

The damage remains.

Broken weapons lie among the shattered paving stones. Sections of the outer wall have collapsed, and the gatehouse is little more than a blackened shell. The courtyard is scattered with abandoned shields, splintered timber and the remains of the Coven's bone-creatures. Soldiers move carefully between them, checking for survivors and gathering the fallen.

You watch them work.

Only yesterday, many of these people were strangers. Now you recognise their faces, their voices and the small habits that have become familiar during the siege. Some are already helping the wounded. Others stand motionless, staring at the destruction as though they have not yet understood that they are alive.

You stand atop the scorched battlements, looking down at the broken tree line where the Coven fled.

Your knuckles are bruised, and your muscles ache from the violent push at the gates. There is a cut along your forearm, and dried blood has gathered beneath one fingernail. You barely notice either.

The keep's banners still fly over the valley.

One is torn almost in half, its edges blackened by fire, but it remains fixed to the pole above the battlements. You look towards the forest beyond it, searching for movement among the trees.

The Coven has retreated. You know better than to mistake that for surrender.

You remember the Coven Leader's final words and the strange pulse beneath the foundations. Whatever began in the woods has not necessarily ended with the siege.

You survived because you refused to yield.

You may need to make that choice again.

You walk the perimeter of the inner sanctum, inspecting the stress cracks in the ancient stone foundations.

The vault anchor held, but the discharge left glowing, hair-thin lines of residual magic etched into the floorboards. They run from the central pillar towards the walls, following the hidden channels beneath the fortress.

You crouch beside one of them.

The light fades when you touch the stone, but you can still feel the current beneath it. The foundation has not been destroyed. It has been disturbed, perhaps more deeply than you intended.

You make a mental note of the damaged sections and the places where the walls will need reinforcement. Rebuilding Highspire's defences will require more than replacing timber and iron. The ancient structure itself needs examining.

For now, the fortress stands.

You intend to understand why.

You move among the makeshift cots lined up in the lower bailey.

The militia you rallied are tired and bruised, but alive. People speak in hushed, reverent tones as you pass, nodding in quiet gratitude. A few reach for your hand. Others simply move aside to let you through.

You stop beside a young guard whose leg has been bound with strips of torn clothing. He tries to sit upright when he recognises you.

“Stay down,” you tell him.

He obeys, though his eyes follow you as you continue along the row.

Mara is helping the local herbalist organise clean cloth and warm water. Tomas has found a hammer and is already working on a broken section of the courtyard railing. Their faces are exhausted, but they are moving, helping wherever they can.

You recognise the same stubborn determination that kept Highspire alive before the siege. It has not disappeared beneath the smoke and rubble.

People are still looking after one another.

A voice interrupts your thoughts.

“You're difficult to find.”

Commander Vane approaches, carrying two battered tin mugs of bitter herbal tea. His armour is dented, and a strip of linen is wrapped around his upper arm. His face is lined with soot and exhaustion, but his gaze is steady.

He hands you one of the mugs.

You take it. The tea is unpleasantly bitter, but its warmth settles into your fingers.

“We survived the night,” Vane says quietly, taking a slow sip. “Which is more than I expected when the ward-breakers hit the outer timber.”

He looks towards the distant tree line.

“But they didn't retreat because they were beaten. They retreated because they accomplished whatever ritual they started in the woods.”

You turn towards him.

“What makes you think they completed it?”

“Their withdrawal was too organised. They weren't running from us. They were leaving once the pressure on the keep had served its purpose.”

He pauses.

“I've seen armies retreat when they've lost. This wasn't that.”

The words settle heavily between you.

You remember the Coven Leader standing beyond the broken gates, the soul-stone pulsing with violet light. You remember its warning that your ancestors had buried something beneath the fortress. The siege may have been intended to weaken the garrison, distract its defenders or force the ancient magic into activity.

Perhaps the attack was never about taking Highspire.

Perhaps it was about making something happen beneath it.

You glance down at your hands.

The faint tremor in your fingers isn't just fatigue. Beneath the ordinary sensations of pain and exhaustion, you can sense something lingering in the groundwater.

It is a subtle disturbance, like a fever spreading through a body before its symptoms become obvious. The Coven's magic has seeped into the soil and water around the garrison. If it reaches the village wells, it could sicken people who have already endured too much.

You think of Elsie and the other children in Highspire.

They survived the fire. They should not have to face another threat simply because the battle has ended.

The contamination needs to be understood and cleansed before it spreads.

Your practiced eye takes in the ruined timber gates and shattered ballista mounts.

The damage is extensive. Several defensive mechanisms have been destroyed, and the outer wall will need substantial repairs before it can withstand another assault.

You notice something else, too.

The old foundations have responded to your bloodline. The magic running through them is powerful, but its structure is not beyond understanding. With the right materials, you could design reinforcements that work alongside the ancient defences rather than relying on iron alone.

Rebuilding Highspire will take weeks.

But you could make it stronger than it was before.

Your eyes scan the muddy tracks leading into the deep forest.

The heavy, irregular prints of the Coven's rearguard are still fresh. You can distinguish the marks of ordinary boots from the deeper impressions left by the creatures that carried their equipment.

The trail leads north-east, towards the wooded slopes.

If anyone were to track them back to their sanctuary, now—before the rain washes away their trail—would be the only chance.

You know the risks. The Coven may have left traps behind, and the survivors could be regrouping with reinforcements. But allowing them to disappear into the forest gives them time to recover.

You look towards the mountains.

The hunt is not over.
A movement near the hearth draws your attention.

Your parents sit wrapped in thick woollen blankets, sipping warm broth and exchanging quiet words with the local herbalist.

Your father looks more tired than you remember seeing him. Your mother has one hand resting over his, and both of them appear smaller beneath the borrowed blankets.

When they notice you watching, your mother gives you a faint smile.

You cross the courtyard and crouch beside them.

“Have you eaten?” she asks.

You almost laugh. The question is so ordinary that it seems to belong to another life.

“Not properly.”

“Then you will.”

Your father looks towards the damaged walls.

“We're still here,” he says.

It is not a declaration of victory. It is a simple statement of fact, and perhaps that makes it more important.

Your younger sibling is fast asleep against a stack of grain sacks, still clutching a small iron rod they carried during the siege.

Their face is smudged with ash, and one hand remains tightly closed around the makeshift weapon. Someone has placed a blanket over their shoulders.

You crouch beside them.

For a moment, you watch the slow rise and fall of their breathing. They look younger asleep, removed from the terror and confusion of the previous night.

You gently ease the iron rod from their fingers and place it beside the sacks.

They stir, then settle again.

You cannot promise that the danger has passed. But you can make sure they have a little longer to rest.

In the quiet corner of the courtyard, your pack sits where you left it—untouched, self-contained and ready for whatever journey comes next.

You look at it for a long moment.

There was a time when the cottage at Highspire's edge was the centre of your world. You knew its creaking roof, its familiar smells and the people who came to your door. Now the village is damaged, the garrison is scarred, and the valley has become part of something far larger than you ever imagined.

You could leave.

There would be no family waiting for you here, no one who could demand that you stay.

But the absence of obligation is not the same as the absence of responsibility.

You turn away from the pack.

For now, there is work to do.

Vane watches you finish the tea.

“The Witan Council will want a full report by nightfall,” he says. “They'll want to know why the Coven attacked, what happened to their leader and what the state of the ancient wards is.”

“And what will you tell them?”

“The truth, as far as I understand it.”

He looks towards the central keep.

“But the valley's future depends on what we do right now. We cannot wait for the Council to decide how to respond. The wounded need attention, the defences need rebuilding, and the Coven is still somewhere beyond those trees.”

He lowers his voice.

“And whatever lies beneath this fortress has not stopped waiting.”

You look across the courtyard.

There are three immediate paths ahead. Each will demand something different from you, and none guarantees safety. The choice will determine whether Highspire spends the coming days healing, preparing or pursuing the enemy.

You take one final sip of the bitter tea and hand the empty mug back to Vane.

The morning is young.

The valley is waiting.
